readings: Using 20.99 as the replacement-cost cutoff, keep only films with replacement_cost strictly greater than 20.99. For each rating, compute the average of rental_rate divided by rental_duration over those films, ignoring missing values. Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it. Show the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean, all unrounded.

Using 20.99 as the replacement-cost cutoff, keep only films with replacement_cost greater than or equal to 20.99, so films at exactly 20.99 are included. For each rating, compute the average of rental_rate divided by rental_duration over those films, ignoring missing values. Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it. Show the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean, all unrounded.
queries:
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio
  FROM film
  WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean
  FROM per_rating
  WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT p.rating,
       p.avg_ratio AS avg_rate_per_day,
       p.avg_ratio - o.overall_mean AS diff_above_mean
FROM per_rating p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL
  AND p.avg_ratio > o.overall_mean;
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio
  FROM film
  WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean
  FROM per_rating
  WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT p.rating,
       p.avg_ratio AS average,
       p.avg_ratio - o.overall_mean AS diff_above_mean
FROM per_rating p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL
  AND p.avg_ratio > o.overall_mean;
